subject: Temporary carve-out request for async filter webhook failures during runtime upgrade
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@novahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@novahealth.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Elevated 504s on filter webhook since your runtime push — requesting carve-out

Hi Marcus,

We rolled a brief test load this morning and started seeing a spike in 504 timeouts from the content-filter webhook after your team’s runtime upgrade (around 08:40 PST). This is impacting a subset of our triage flows where we call back out to our moderation toolchain; the end-user latencies are courting our SLA thresholds.

Attached is a small slice of the incident logs (filter-incident-log.csv) showing ~18 minutes of elevated 504/524 errors and retry storms from our workers. Our SREs are asking whether Redwood can provide a temporary SLA carve-out or an alternative routing (e.g., route affected traffic to the previous model build) while you complete the rollback or patch.

High level ask: an explicit carve-out window (start/end), acceptance criteria (error rate back to baseline), and any credit/backup plan. We’re on a tight timeline — our ops leadership has asked for a formal note by EOD PT.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Director, Platform Reliability
Nova Health Systems
---
Attachments: filter-incident-log.csv (csv, 42KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@novahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 504s on filter webhook since your runtime push — requesting carve-out

Hi Sara — thanks for the quick heads-up and for sending the logs. I’m looking through the slices you attached.

Quick summary from our side: we rolled a micro-optimization to the KV cache handling and kernel selection at ~08:35 PST which changed the steady-state memory layout for a small class of transformer instances. In most traffic patterns this improves latency, but we’re seeing an unexpected interaction with certain async webhook timeouts where a backlog triggered temporary lock contention and delayed tool-calls.

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
- Neha (cc’d) will validate whether the observed 504 pattern is tied to the webhook client timeouts vs. internal filter stalls.
- We can provisionally redirect the affected webhook route to the previous runtime snapshot (we have a snapshot that can serve with previous kernel selection) — that would require a short config flip and warmup (~20–30 minutes).
- If you’d prefer a formal carve-out, we can draft limited language: a time-boxed SLA exception for the affected ingestion path tied to the upgrade window and with explicit rollback/monitoring acceptance criteria.

I’m looping in Jordan from commercial to make sure the carve-out language aligns with the contract and to document any credits. Neha — can you confirm feasibility of the config flip and whether there’s any data retention or observability constraints we should include?

I’ll hold off on the config flip until I hear back from you (so we don’t oscillate mid-mitigation).

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0162

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@novahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@novahealth.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 504s on filter webhook since your runtime push — requesting carve-out

Thanks Marcus — we’re OK with a timeboxed carve-out if it’s narrow and tied to the upgrade window. Our concerns:
- We need clear start/end times, with automated rollback triggers if error rate remains above 0.5% for >15 minutes.
- We prefer minimal scope: only the async webhook route to the moderation toolchain, not a global SLA change.
- We need monitoring dashboards and a public incident link we can reference for our ops runbooks.

If you can send a short proposed carve-out doc with wording we can run through our procurement, that would help expedite EOD acceptance on our side. I attached a short set of additional log slices per your request.

Sara
Sara Patel
Director, Platform Reliability
Nova Health Systems
---
Attachments: filter-incident-log-part2.csv (csv, 18KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@novahealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 14:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 504s on filter webhook since your runtime push — requesting carve-out

Sara, Marcus — I dug into the traces and reproduced the lock contention pattern in a small perf harness. We can perform the config flip to the prior runtime snapshot and route Nova's webhook traffic there. Estimated timeline: 25 minutes to flip + 20 minutes warmup to re-populate caches.

I’ve drafted a short carve-out term and attached it as proposed-carveout-term.docx. Key elements:
- Scope: async moderation webhook endpoint only (endpoint: /v1/moderation/async; traffic from Nova account ID).
- Window: Nov 2, 2027 08:30 PST — Nov 2, 2027 12:00 PST (provisional; actual window begins at config flip time).
- Acceptance criteria: stabilized error rate <0.5% sustained for 30 minutes; otherwise automatic rollback to previous config and full incident postmortem.
- Credits: proportionate to the percentage of requests impacted during the window (to be confirmed with Jordan/legal).
- Monitoring: link to a live dashboard (see below) and a post-incident SLO report within 48 hours.

Jordan — can you confirm commercial language and whether we need a formal amendment vs. a signed acceptance? Sara — attaching the doc and the dashboard link.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Applied ML Ops
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
---
Attachments: proposed-carveout-term.docx (docx, 12KB)
Live dashboard: https://internal.grayboard.redwood.com/dashboards/NOVA-FILTER-5892

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@novahealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 16:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 504s on filter webhook since your runtime push — requesting carve-out

Sara — thanks for the fast collaboration here and for being specific about scope. We can accept the proposed carve-out terms as an addendum to the existing MSA for the Nova Health Systems account (DEAL-5892). Two quick notes from commercial/legal:
- We’ll record the carve-out as a limited amendment (no term extension) and include the acceptance criteria you requested. No credits will be processed until the post-incident review confirms impacted volume; we will provisionally reserve a credit bucket that will be reconciled in the postmortem.
- Please reply to this thread with explicit acceptance of the scope + the requested rollback trigger thresholds and we’ll generate the signed addendum.

Per Neha — the config flip is scheduled for tonight at 23:20 PST to minimize user impact. Marcus will confirm when the route is flipped and provide the incident dashboard link.

If we get your acceptance now we’ll prepare the addendum and send a DocuSign link.

—Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Accepted terms (pending signature): see attached proposed-carveout-term.docx
Monitoring: https://internal.grayboard.redwood.com/dashboards/NOVA-FILTER-5892
